findings.title: Alt-dragging a frame to duplicate it puts the copied arrow's end somewhere that depends on how many pointer moves the drag took, when the arrow is bound to an element in another frame
findings.observed: Setup: frame A (0,0,300x300) holds rectA, frame B holds rectB at x=600, and an arrow in frame A runs from rectA (100,150) to rectB (650,150). Alt-dragging frame A from (250,250) to (250,550) in one pointer move leaves the duplicate arrow's end at (650,150). The same drag done in two moves (y=400, then 550) leaves it at (650,300), and in three moves (300, 350, 550) at (650,400). The end is unbound each time. The end lags by the offset of the first move.
findings.expected: Alt-dragging frame A to the same final pointer position should give the same result however many pointer moves the drag took. The duplicated arrow's end should either stay on rectB at (650,150) or move the full drag offset with the duplicate frame to (650,450).

findings.title: "Bring forward" on an element just below a frame jumps it past unrelated elements when that frame has a deleted child higher in the stack
findings.observed: Saved order after Bring forward was childB, frameF, rectX, ellipseE. ellipseE skipped over the unrelated rectX and landed where the deleted child A had been. This happened in 4 of 4 runs. In the control (same scene, but A has frameId null before it is deleted) the order is childB, frameF, ellipseE, rectX. This is the same deleted-children-keep-frameId problem the commit fixed for insertion, but in z-index moves (getContiguousFrameRangeElements doesn't skip isDeleted). It probably predates this commit.
findings.expected: Once child A is deleted, frame F's group is only [childB, frameF]. Bring forward (Ctrl+]) on ellipseE, which sits just below that group, should place it directly above frameF: childB, frameF, ellipseE, rectX. A control scene where A is not a frame child gives exactly that order.

findings.title: Alt+arrow flowchart navigation selects a locked node, so Delete (or other edits) then removes the locked element
findings.observed: Scene: A at (0,0), locked B at (300,0) in A's row, C at (0,300), elbow arrows A→C→B (B is not linked to A directly). With A selected, Alt+ArrowRight made selectedElementIds = {lockedB}. Delete then set lockedB.isDeleted=true. 3 of 3 runs. A locked node linked directly to A behaves the same way (seen once while exploring); the old code also followed direct links. Reaching an unlinked node in the same row is new with this commit's visual navigation.
findings.expected: Locked elements can't be selected, the same as with clicking or Ctrl+A. Alt+arrow should skip a locked node or do nothing, and pressing Delete should leave the locked element in place.
